status: design complete; implementation and hardware validation pending
problem: FreeMKV normal MTK probe requires MMC feature 0x010C; affected ASUS BW-16D1HT BOOT returns 8-byte empty feature response and is rejected before writes. MTK has no RecoveryFacet implementation.
entry: Implement RecoveryFacet on Mtk and expose it via Backend::recovery; preserve ordinary flash detection policy.
identify: Read INQUIRY independent of normal backend probe. BOOT revision is evidence of recovery state, not sufficient controller proof.
Read MT1959 boot banner and bounded receiver code windows using the inspected boot READ BUFFER route; log exact CDB, length, status and sense.
Fingerprint plaintext ASUS vs encrypted INTM/V9 receiver from actual code; do not infer transport from target filename or current application descriptor.
Missing 0x010C, serial feature, damaged application descriptor and absent full backup must not prevent recovery identification.
plan: Validate target size, chip/banner, CMAC, raw-read versus stored-image form, and receiver-specific descriptor/marker gates.
Use receiver/hardware evidence for compatibility; do not require old and new application identities to agree.
No backup or partial capture in recovery; read only for receiver identification, validation and result verification.
Preview chosen payload, transport, preservation ranges and evidence before writing.
No target-as-installed substitution: add recovery-specific preparation API to mediatek-optical if reusing PreparedUpdate.
execute: Reuse verified WRITE BUFFER sequence, but choose transport from active receiver.
Preserve boot by default; same-chip banner may cause receiver to clear requested boot-update flag.
Follow per-unit preservation behavior only after tracing actual flash primitive.
Wait for readiness then re-read INQUIRY and descriptor; remaining BOOT is incomplete recovery, not success.
Re-identify receiver between stages; do not automatically send encrypted V9 if INTM never started.

paths.second: original encrypted V9 payload from pcupdate891.bin after running INTM is confirmed

paths.unknown: Actual retained ASUS boot revision; hardware startup compatibility and write acceptance.

INQUIRY plus boot banner and receiver code reads with sense responses

scope_order: Automatic plaintext/encrypted selection shared by normal flash and recovery
User flashes INTM and confirms successful startup, then separately flashes V9 with fresh automatic selection

automatic_transport.result: Plaintext, Aes128Ecb, or Unknown; no implicit plaintext fallback
inputs: Live INQUIRY and current operating state
Live receiver code fingerprint when readable
Verified installed image/profile bound to live identity when application code cannot be read directly
policy: Select based on active receiver, not target file revision or filename
BOOT state uses boot receiver; running INTM uses its application receiver even when ASUS boot persists
Target image stays canonical plaintext for integrity validation and verification; transform only outgoing transfer buffer
Re-read binding evidence before execute to prevent stale plans
Unknown reports what evidence is missing rather than presenting a guess as detection
validation: Original OEM encrypted V9 payload must decrypt to canonical V9 and be reproduced by selected transform
Plaintext ASUS/old V1 and encrypted INTM/V9 receiver fixtures
Same target encoded differently for different receivers
Normal and recovery routes share selection result
Post-INTM V9 operation starts with fresh probe
profile_strategy: Profiles distinguish boot receivers from application receivers and include readable code fingerprints, transport encoding, marker/sentinel checks and writable regions.
Prefer live code fingerprint; fallback only to an audited exact installed identity/build profile bound to live non-BOOT metadata. Never use a blanket model/date cutoff to infer encryption.
No trial write, wrong-format retry, or encrypt-on-error fallback. Unknown needs additional receiver support, not a toggle.
Host may accept validated plaintext or recognized encrypted firmware input, but always decode to canonical plaintext first; receiver selection independently controls outgoing format.

read_only_probe: probe_mtk_boot.py captures BOOT inquiry, omitted feature, boot code windows, descriptor and calibration sample on Windows; opcode allowlist excludes writes. Local packet-layout and allowlist checks passed; Windows/hardware run not yet performed.

platforms.implementation: Shared Rust protocol logic through ScsiDevice -> libfreemkv::scsi transport adapter (SPTI, IOKit, SG_IO). Same decisions for CLI and GUI.
platforms.windows_probe: Research-only diagnostic helper, not a product dependency or required workflow.

ownership.mediatek-optical: Receiver profiles, input acceptance predicates, transport encoding and validated update/recovery plan. Proposed ReceiverProfile/TransportEncoding/ReceiverEvidence and recovery-specific prepare API.
ownership.freemkv-flash: Acquire live receiver evidence through ScsiDevice, expose info diagnostics, bind/revalidate plans, implement Mtk RecoveryFacet, execute and verify through shared engine.
ownership.CLI and GUI: Present the same backend capabilities and operation result; no frontend protocol heuristics or encoding switches.

frontend_changes: Recover input must accept a MediaTek 2 MiB image, not require Pioneer Kernel+Normal wording.
Make current-firmware input backend-dependent: optional for MediaTek when live boot evidence suffices. Preserve Pioneer requirements.
Expose Recovery when its receiver matches, even if ordinary flash classification is Unknown.
Show selected transfer encoding and evidence as read-only plan details.
After recovering INTM, refresh drive profile; user selects V9 in a separate normal flash operation.

user_path.behavior: Recognize actual ASUS BOOT receiver without 0x010C; automatically select its transport (plaintext for the inspected ASUS receivers); validate INTM, preview, and execute on explicit user action.
user_path.success: INQUIRY changes from BOOT to BH16NS40 INTM, stable readiness plus supported readback verification. If it remains BOOT or verification fails, stop and record sense/status.

user_path.behavior: Fresh identification recognizes the running INTM application profile; automatically wrap canonical V9 with AES-128-ECB. No encryption control or manual .enc preparation. Revalidate receiver before sending.
user_path.success: INQUIRY reports WH16NS58 1.V9, stable readiness and supported readback verification. No automatic second flash or retry.

evidence_summary: Affected log proves host classification refusal before firmware writes.
OEM updater sends plaintext INTM then encrypted V9 for the stocked V1 date.
ASUS BOOT code includes READ BUFFER and WRITE BUFFER handlers.
INTM application performs crypto transform before header checks.
All CMAC table entries verify for supplied INTM and V9.
AES-128-ECB encoding canonical V9 reproduces original OEM transport payload byte-for-byte (transport-proof.json).
implementation_acceptance: All transport and recovery logic shared across Windows/macOS/Linux; existing per-OS adapter remains sole OS boundary.
Normal flash and recovery call one selector; no internal bypass that silently forces plaintext.
Golden receiver vectors cover both encodings and wrong/unknown state; canonical V9 encryption exactly matches OEM.
BOOT without 0x010C identified through receiver evidence; unrelated BOOT devices never selected by name alone.
Dry run and identification produce no firmware-write commands.
Recovery tolerates broken application metadata and missing restorable backup; does not save a backup or partial capture.
Reject corrupt/incompatible target or marker failure with precise receiver-specific cause.
Stale receiver state after planning invalidates execute.
INTM running state required before user proceeds to V9; final BOOT state never counted as success.
Platform CI compiles/tests shared flow and frontend parity; physical-drive test needed before advertising proven recovery.
